transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Isabel Chen (Borealis Head Cloud Ops), Marcus Doyle (Borealis CISO), Priya Singh (Borealis Compliance)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand Borealis Trust constraints around KMS residency, log retention and redaction, tenant isolation for multi-tenant workloads, and whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated or Private fit their compliance posture. High-level ask: can Redwood guarantee no plaintext prompt storage outside EU region, support BYOK via HSM/KMS, and provide log redaction before long-term storage for audit?

Topics covered:
- KMS/BYOK & HSM requirements
- Log capture, redaction, retention windows
- Tenant isolation and evidence for auditors
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for financial services
- Next steps: SOC2/HIPAA artifacts, runbook, pilot pricing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Alright, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick sound check?
[00:05] Isabel Chen: Hi, sound good. Isabel here.
[00:07] Marcus Doyle: Marcus, loud and clear.
[00:09] Priya Singh: Priya, on my side too.
[00:12] Ethan Liu: Ethan from Redwood, hey all.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Cool. So the goal today is to map Borealis' security and ops constraints. We'll take notes and then propose a path — hosted, dedicated or private. Marcus, can you kick us off with the compliance must-haves?
[00:28] Marcus Doyle: Sure. So primary — we are regulated trust services, need strong data residency in EU, GDPR compliance, plus some UK-specific controls. HIPAA isn't a primary requirement but we do have PHI-like fields in some docs and may need BAA for specific pilots.
[00:42] Marcus Doyle: The big ask is keys: we cannot have provider-managed keys outside our control. BYOK, ideally HSM backed, with key residency in our cloud tenant. We also need audit evidence of key usage.
[00:55] Priya Singh: And on logs: we need the ability to redact PII before logs go into long-term object storage. Short-term transient logs for debugging ok, but they should be automatically purged, and only redacted/aggregated records kept for more than 30 days.
[01:12] Isabel Chen: Also, we run a shared tenant model internally — any Redwood deployment must give us strong logical tenant isolation and the ability to carve off dedicated pools for higher-risk workloads. So multi-tenant defaults are fine if cryptographic isolation and network boundaries are present.
[01:28] Ethan Liu: Thanks — that helps. Quick clarifying question: when you say "audit evidence of key usage" — do you need HSM-level attestation (e.g., Cloud HSM logs) or is KMS API access logs sufficient?
[01:40] Marcus Doyle: KMS API logs are baseline. For high-risk workloads we'd like attestation. If Redwood supports connecting to our KMS or HSM as the key store (BYOK), that's preferable.
[01:52] Maya Patel: Good — so BYOK + KMS integration is a priority. On hosted mode, we do support BYOK via customer-managed KMS keys in certain regions, and an HSM-backed flow for Dedicated/Private. Ethan, can you speak to the key flow?
[02:05] Ethan Liu: Yeah. For Redwood Hosted we have an option where customers bring keys in Cloud KMS (we call it BYOK path) — Redwood requests short-lived envelopes and does not persist plaintext key material. For Dedicated and Private, we can either integrate into the customer's VPC KMS endpoint or run in their on-prem HSM. However, the hosted path has caveats around full audit attestation — some attestation materials are available but not HSM attestation in some regions.
[02:32] Priya Singh: That caveat matters. If we can't get attestation for Hosted, we might need Dedicated. How about logs? Hosted by default stores transcripts for 90 days for debugging — can that be shortened and redaction applied?
[02:45] Ethan Liu: We can configure retention in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has configurable retention but there are platform constraints. We also support on-the-fly redaction hooks — you can supply a set of redaction rules or use an agent that strips PII before logs are persisted. Note: these redaction hooks run before long-term storage but may appear in short-term ephemeral logging for 24-72 hours depending on system traces.
[03:10] Isabel Chen: What's "on-the-fly redaction hooks" exactly? Is that something in the customer's side or Redwood's runtime?
[03:15] Ethan Liu: It's a pipeline we offer where a redaction plugin executes in the request path — essentially a configured filter step that normalizes and masks tokens matching rules before the request gets stored in object storage or observability backends. For Dedicated/Private we can put that filter inside the VPC so raw prompts never leave the customer boundary.
[03:30] Marcus Doyle: Do you have controls to prevent kernel memory or kv cache dumps from leaking sensitive tokens into logs? We saw issues with some runtimes where kv cache contents were recorded in traces.
[03:41] Ethan Liu: Good point. Our runtime has modes that limit kv cache dumping for traces and we can disable verbose tracing in production. For audits we can provide sanitized traces and justify that debugging traces do not contain full prompt content. I'll note that as a required deliverable.
[03:56] Maya Patel: For regulatory evidence — Marcus/ Priya — would a SOC2 Type II report plus architecture diagrams and a runbook showing key flows be sufficient to sign off on a POC?
[04:07] Priya Singh: That would cover most. We also need to review the BAA language if we have PHI in any flow. And we will want to see RBAC controls, SSO/SAML integration, and just-in-time access logs for operations.
[04:21] Maya Patel: Redwood supports SSO via SAML/Okta and RBAC with granularity for token-level ops. For audit logs we emit admin actions, token creates, and model rollout events. Ethan, any notes on admin/audit log retention?
[04:33] Ethan Liu: Admin audit logs are configurable. Hosted: 90 days default, extendable as an add-on. Dedicated/Private: you control retention and can ship logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders. We can also support region-locked log sinks to keep logs within EU.
[04:50] Isabel Chen: Important: our auditors will ask for chain of custody for logs. So we need signed hashes or an evidence trail. Do you do log signing?
[04:59] Ethan Liu: We don't do signed hashes out-of-the-box currently, but we can provide immutable object storage configuration guidance and integrate with customer-side signing in the pipeline. That's a rare ask but doable in Dedicated/Private.
[05:12] Marcus Doyle: Pricing/tradeoffs question — sounds like Private gives us the strongest guarantees. What are the main differences in cost and ops between Dedicated and Private from your view?
[05:22] Maya Patel: Short answer: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware reserved for you inside our regions — we handle patching and some ops, you get predictable capacity and better isolation. Private is fully customer-managed control plane or on-prem — more engineering on your side but maximum control. Pricing: Dedicated is mid-tier, Private is premium due to support and deployment complexity. We'll send a pricing sketch.
[05:41] Priya Singh: We also require the ability to run periodic vulnerability scans and to receive scan reports. Is that compatible?
[05:47] Ethan Liu: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we can allow scheduled scans on the customer-owned network boundary; on Hosted we provide our own vulnerability attestations and scanner reports but don't expose internal hosts.
[05:58] Isabel Chen: One more: can Redwood guarantee that raw prompts won't be replicated to third-party analytics vendors? We use a set of analytics tools and want assurance that PII is never forwarded.
[06:08] Ethan Liu: We don't sell customer data. Integrations that forward telemetry (e.g., metrics exporters) are opt-in; we can configure filters to strip PII. For Hosted, integrations are optional and documented. We'll call this out in the security pack.
[06:24] Maya Patel: Good. Technical deep dive requests — Marcus, do you want a timeline for an SE-led feasibility that includes a network diagram review?
[06:31] Marcus Doyle: Yes please, an SE-led session where we walk through our VPC, KMS endpoints, and sample data flows. Also Marcus: we may want a short bench where you run synthetic loads to validate latencies under our expected token mix.
[06:42] Ethan Liu: We can do both. For benchmarking we'll need sample prompt shapes and token counts. We can run a small in-region bench on Dedicated or a Private pre-prod to model costs.
[06:53] Priya Singh: On the redaction side, can you do pattern-based and ML-based redaction? Some of our records are semi-structured and patterns won't catch everything.
[07:03] Ethan Liu: We support both pattern-based (regex rules) and a configured ML redact step — the ML step runs inside the VPC for Private/Dedicated; for Hosted the ML step can run either in-region or via a managed plugin with stronger safeguards. There is a small false positive/negative tradeoff that we can quantify on sample data.
[07:24] Isabel Chen: Any limitations we should know about for realtime redaction latency? We have a latency SLO of <300ms 95 for certain flows.
[07:32] Ethan Liu: Redaction adds overhead. Pattern-based is negligible (<10-20ms typically). ML-based redaction could add 30-80ms depending on model. We can tune via async post-processing in lower SLO flows or smart sampling for logs.
[07:49] Maya Patel: OK, sounds like action items forming. Before we recap, any other security or procurement items?
[07:55] Marcus Doyle: Contract: we require breach notification windows and specific SLA clauses around key compromise. Also want to see indemnity language aligned with our counsel — we'll send redlines later.
[08:06] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll share standard legal templates and can iterate.
[08:10] Priya Singh: Also, please include a short checklist of required artifacts for auditor review — e.g., SOC2, BAA, KMS integration diagram, runbooks, RBAC screenshots.
[08:20] Maya Patel: We'll include that. Recap and next steps:
[08:24] Maya Patel: 1) Redwood to share SOC2 Type II, security pack including KMS integration notes and redaction docs by 2026-07-02.
[08:33] Maya Patel: 2) Ethan to schedule a 60–90 minute SE-led feasibility with Marcus to review VPC/KMS and run a shallow bench — target week of 2026-07-06.
[08:45] Maya Patel: 3) AE to prepare pilot estimate and pricing for Dedicated and Private options by 2026-07-05.
[08:52] Isabel Chen: We'll also share our log retention policy and sample data shapes for the redaction tests by 2026-07-03.
[08:59] Marcus Doyle: Good. One ask: when you send docs, flag any items that are caveats for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private so our security team doesn't miss them.
[09:09] Ethan Liu: Will do. We'll label hosted caveats clearly.
[09:12] Maya Patel: Great. Anything else?
[09:14] Priya Singh: No, that covers it. Thanks.
[09:17] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links.
[09:21] End of recording.

References mentioned (links/names to include in follow-up):
